text: One day a traveling peasant. <break time="0.8s" /> Told Pahom about a place. <break time="0.8s" /> Beyond the Volga. <break time="0.8s" /> Where each man received twenty five acres. <break time="0.8s" /> The land there was so rich. <break time="0.8s" /> He said. <break time="0.8s" /> That the rye grew as tall as a horse. <break time="0.8s" /> Why should I suffer. <break time="0.8s" /> In this narrow place. <break time="0.8s" /> Pahom thought. <break time="0.8s" /> If I could live so well over there. <break time="0.8s" /> So he sold his land. <break time="0.8s" /> And moved his family to the new place. <break time="0.8s" /> Where they got a hundred and twenty five acres. <break time="0.8s" /> He was ten times better off than before but after a while. <break time="0.8s" /> Even this land did not seem enough. <break time="0.8s" /> He wanted to grow more wheat. <break time="0.8s" /> So he rented extra land every year. <break time="0.8s" /> Which often led to quarrels. <break time="0.8s" /> If the land were my own. <break time="0.8s" /> He thought. <break time="0.8s" /> I would be free. <break time="0.8s" /> And there would be no more trouble. <break time="0.8s" /> A peasant agreed to sell him. <break time="0.8s" /> Thirteen hundred acres for fifteen hundred rubles. <break time="0.8s" /> And the deal was almost settled. <break time="0.8s" /> Just then. <break time="0.8s" /> A passing dealer told him about the Bashkirs. <break time="0.8s" /> A simple people living far away. <break time="0.8s" /> He said that he had bought thirteen thousand acres from them. <break time="0.8s" /> For only a thousand rubles.
